intro: You heard it too, didn't you? The bell beneath the woods. It has not rung since my grandmother was a girl.
And now the goblins are gathering around the shrine.
The roots have gone dark. Even your wolf can smell it. Bring me three Moonleaf sprigs; their light will open the old sanctuary.
We'll find what woke beneath Willowbrook.
Follow the northern trail, cross Sunstream, and look for the purple flowers. Come back before entering the ruin.
herbs: All three! Hold still. A little moonlight, a little courage... there.
Take these potions. Follow Whisperwood north, cross Sunstream into Sunmeadow Plains, then reach the shrine at the far end of the road. Below are two seals, guarded by creatures and puzzles.
Break the seals, then find the source?
Yes. But the guardian was once our protector. If it draws back its branches, raise your guard. Do not meet that blow head-on.
reminder: Three purple Moonleaf plants: two in Whisperwood, one on the plains beyond Sunstream. They are marked purple on your map. Your wolf will keep you company.
ready: The Moonleaf charm will open the shrine across Sunstream. Find both root seals below, then wake the guardian from its nightmare.
shrine: These carvings... a guardian sheltering the village beneath its branches.
Remember what we protect. That is the oath, not the sword.
Then let's bring our guardian home.
sealed: The stone door is alive with black roots. Mira may know how to loosen them. We should finish gathering Moonleaf first.
dungeon: The air is colder here. Two chambers, two seals. Stone dials to the west and old bells to the east. Their inscriptions must tell us how to wake them.
The wolf's ears prick toward the darkness. Somewhere below, wood creaks like a ship at sea.
seal: The roots loosen. A little light is finding its way back.
Your companion nudges your hand, then watches the northern passage.
boss_locked: Two root seals bind the guardian. We need to cleanse both side chambers before the heart will open.
boss: I remember a bell. Children tied ribbons to my branches. Why do I remember their hands as axes?
The bell is still ringing above us. Someone wanted you to hear a threat instead of a welcome.
My roots hold this village together. If I unclench them, everything falls.
Then let me stand here when you do. You don’t have to hold it alone.
Come close, little promise. Show me something that does not break.
boss_win: There. A bird. I had forgotten how small their feet were.
You stopped listening for the axe.
No. I heard it, and heard the bird as well. There is room for both.
Take this ember from my heartwood. The water keeper carried our first oath east. Ask why the royal seal appears on a promise older than the crown.
I’ll ask. And I’ll come back when the ribbons are up.
ending: The stream is clear again. I knew before I saw you.
The guardian was trapped. Something deeper was pulling at its roots.
Then there will be another road, another day. For now, you brought our forest back.
I'd say it has only just begun.
epilogue: Listen. Birds, the stream, your wolf pretending not to want another treat. I could get used to this kind of quiet.
So could I. For a little while.
marsh_royal: Mira sent word of the restored guardian. His Majesty came to Reedcross when the waterworks failed. He asked to hear from you personally.
You helped Willowbrook without a crown to command you. That is the sort of service this realm needs.
I have opened the royal granary to Reedcross. But grain cannot mend its failing sluices. Speak to Warden Iona; listen before you draw your weapon.
The forest guardian was wounded by a broken oath. Could these waters share its roots?
Then help me keep an older promise: no village abandoned to the flood. Take this travel purse. I will remain until the evacuation boats are ready.
marsh_iona: The ancient waterworks are drowning our fields. Blue lanterns burn where no ferryman walks, and the keeper no longer hears us.
Bring a water-reading from each of the three blue survey stones along the causeway. They will tell us whether the seal is broken or merely blocked.
marsh_key: All three readings point inward. The keeper is trapping the flood to protect a covenant nobody remembers.
Take this sluice key. In the reliquary: drain the west basin, cross its bed, then divert the east channel. Do not mistake an open valve for a safe crossing.
The inscription says: EMPTY the bowl; TURN the river; QUIET the heart. Listen when the keeper gathers a tide.
marsh_after: The channels are running clear. You did not destroy our keeper; you freed it from an oath twisted against the people it protected.
My soldiers will repair the causeway. You have my thanks—and payment, not merely praise.
The tablet names an Emberglass archive in the Sahir desert. Someone removed a passage about the first closing of the gates.
The eastern caravan road is open. Seek your answers in Sahir; I will see the causeway repaired.
marsh_complete: The eastern caravan road is open. Look for its sign east of our square. Qasira’s archivist knows the Emberglass Tomb.
marsh_reeds: My patients cannot wait for the flood to fall. I need four silverreed bundles from the marked banks along the causeway. Watch for leeches by the water.
marsh_patrol: Reed Stalkers have taken the causeway. Defeat three and I can bring the medicine boat through. You can clear them before or after speaking to me.
marsh_boss_before: State your name. State your cargo. State which of your dead you would leave at the gate.
None. I came to open it.
Every king says that. The last brought chains under white cloth. I kept the water out until they ordered me to keep the people in.
Iona’s people still live above you. Your oath is drowning them.
Then prove you can bear a tide without becoming a wall.
marsh_boss_after: The names on my shield… I thought they were prisoners. They were the people I ferried home.
You can remember them without keeping everyone else here.
An archivist in Qasira kept a glass copy of the covenant. The copy was never delivered to the throne.
Then that’s where we go next.
Take the dry road. I will mind the river. This time, the gates stay open.
sahir_intro: You’ve brought marsh mud into my desert. That is either commitment or a very expensive wrong turn.
The keeper sent me. He said you had a copy of the first covenant.
I had a rubbing. Namarra took the original into her tomb when the sky turned to glass. She believes every visitor is another royal collector.
Then arrive with knowledge instead of a seal. Read the oasis, wreck and observatory inscriptions. Each holds a direction the mirrors have forgotten.
sahir_key: East for dawn, west for dusk, south for the moon. Three memories; one sky. The tomb should let you pass now.
She was keeper of the caravan skies. Her glass wings kept storms from the road. Do not mistake her fear for cruelty.
Good. But take supplies. Being understood sometimes takes a second attempt.
sahir_after: You came back with every bone inside your skin. I owe Laleh a coin.
Namarra said the oath was forged, not signed.
Kharholt. The Ironroot foundry stamped the royal seal on the covenant. Follow the northeastern pass; Brann can read the hammer marks.
sahir_tablet_0: At the oasis: “DAWN reaches EAST. We gave travelers a horizon, not a border.” I’ll remember that.
sahir_tablet_1: The broken caravan plaque reads: “DUSK faces WEST. Count the people who arrive, never the coins they carry.”
sahir_tablet_2: In the observatory: “The MOON looks SOUTH, toward the living.” Someone scratched a royal crest beneath the older writing.
sahir_boss_before: No more lanterns. No more hooks. I have no feathers left for your king.
I’m not here to take your wings. I need to know what happened to the covenant.
They polished my scales until I could see only their faces. They called that loyalty.
Safiya remembers the sky before the storms. So do the caravans.
Then look at me without looking away. When the light breaks, stand your ground.
sahir_boss_after: You shielded your eyes. You did not reach for a broken scale.
Some things don’t belong in a trophy room.
The covenant was not signed. It was struck on an anvil beneath Kharholt. The first seal closed a wound. The second made a weapon of it.
Ask Vorr. He still kneels beneath the weight of the answer. The highland pass is yours.
kharholt_intro: Keep your fingers away from the anvil. It remembers being hot longer than a visitor remembers being warned.
Namarra sent me. I’m looking for Vorr and the first royal seal.
Of course you are. Everyone wants a king’s secret; nobody wants to carry the coal.
Three forge songs survive at the overlook, storm ruins and miners’ camp. Bring them back. They are instructions, not music. Vorr will know if you skip a verse.
kharholt_key: Cool the west anvil. Vent the east. Never open both while the heart is burning. That’s the song.
Why did they hide it outside?
So one frightened keeper could not lock the whole mountain. Watchers hold the valve keys. Vorr holds everything else.
Especially that. Take a proper weapon. A promise won’t turn aside his hammer.
kharholt_after: The chimney smoke is silver again. For the first time in years, it smells like work instead of a warning.
Vorr said the crown and the gate were made from the same iron.
Then the next question is who has been feeding the furnace. Rest here. The mountain is open to you, and there are still lost camps worth finding.
kharholt_tablet_0: The overlook stone reads: “First, cool the western anvil. Iron bends; a trapped heart breaks.”
kharholt_tablet_1: The storm tower remembers: “Second, vent the eastern pressure. Give the mountain somewhere to breathe.”
kharholt_tablet_2: The miners carved their names below the last verse: “Leave no worker beneath the stone.” Vorr’s name is last.
kharholt_boss_before: The shift is not finished. The names have not all been called.
Brann sent me to relieve you.
Brann was a child when the roof fell. He used to bring me a cup of water. I could never hold it.
He remembers. He wants you out of here.
If I stand, the mountain moves. If I kneel, the furnace eats. Tell me which promise I am allowed to break.
The one that says you have to choose alone.
kharholt_boss_after: Listen. No hammer. No falling stone. Just… wind.
The west anvil is cold. The east vent is open. You can stand.
The crown and the gate came from one iron bloom. Every time the seal is renewed, the king asks the mountain for another piece of itself.
Aldren called it repairing an old defense.
A blade is a defense until someone tells it where to point. Keep asking who holds the hilt.
I will. But first, Brann owes you a cup of water.
